open.why: The document describes three 10 kΩ pots on A0-A2, three 220 Ω resistors on D3/D5/D6 and an RGB LED. circuit.json holds a breadboard, an Arduino Uno, ONE potentiometer, a vcc and a gnd: no resistor of any value, and no LED. The assert block passes because it asserts only the rail and that one pot's wiper, so the example is enrolled as `kind: full` with a green physics gate over a bench that cannot show what the page says. It is one of fourteen arduino-sk-* examples with a stubbed bench (p07 through p14 hold nothing but an Uno, a vcc and a gnd), which is why it is recorded here rather than repaired in this lane: building out fourteen starter-kit benches is its own piece of work, and doing one of them would leave the gate green over the other thirteen.

open.verdict: THE DOCUMENT IS WRONG — PENDING CONFIRMATION FROM THE bw-board LANE
open.why: "Transistor saturates (V_CE ~ 0.2 V)" asserts saturation without establishing it. Measured on 88e9668 with the button closed: base 0.6957 V, collector 0.6957 V, emitter 0, so V_CE = 0.6957 V — not 0.2. I_B = (5 - 0.6957)/10000 = 0.4304 mA and beta*I_B = 43.04 mA, which is exactly what the collector carries, so the device sits at the edge of the active region rather than in saturation. Its neighbour 38-npn-switch makes the same argument CORRECTLY — "saturated (V_CE ~ 0.2 V) since 5.96 mA << 43 mA" — and the engine confirms that one at 0.2006 V, which is why this is read as an assertion rather than a derivation. OPEN QUESTION, put to the bw-board lane before any document is edited: the buzzer drops 4.30 V at 43 mA, i.e. presents about 100 ohm. If that is not the intended piezo impedance the transistor WOULD saturate, the document would be right about the physics, and the fix would belong to the bench or the device model instead. Also noted there: buzz1's branchCurrent reads 0.0000 mA while its own net carries 43 mA, so the buzzer has no branchCurrents hook — irrelevant to this verdict, which rests on node voltages, but it is a KCL-invisible part.
